question.worked_solution:
We start by changing the variable:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =2{x}^{3}+4 \\ \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =6{x}^{2} \\ \text{d}u & =6{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u & =3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we create a table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=2{x}^{3}+4.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 1 & 2 \\ u & 6 & 20\end{aligned}
$$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{2{x}^{3}+4}\cdot 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{6}^{20}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we can solve it and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{6}^{20}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{6}^{20}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(u){|}_{6}^{20} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(20)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{20}{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{10}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$
